problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -7 & 10 \\ -9 & -1 & -6 & 9 \\ -2 & 2 & 2 & -6 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 & -7\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{32}$ equal to zero.*

activity_context.topic_title: Finding Determinants Using Row and Column Operations

feedback.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 6 & -3 \\ 3 & -3 & 7 & -2 \\ 5 & -2 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & -4 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{43}$ equal to zero.*
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{43}=-1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 6 & -3 \\ 3 & -3 & 7 & -2 \\ 5 & -2 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & -4 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+2{C}_{3} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+(-4){C}_{3} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+(-3){C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}14 & -20 & 6 & -21 \\ 17 & -31 & 7 & -23 \\ 3 & 2 & -1 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $4$th row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}14 & -20 & 6 & -21 \\ 17 & -31 & 7 & -23 \\ 3 & 2 & -1 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)^{4+3}|\begin{aligned}14 & -20 & -21 \\ 17 & -31 & -23 \\ 3 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}14 & -20 & -21 \\ 17 & -31 & -23 \\ 3 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
